actors.name: Primeiro Comando da Capital
actors.description: Brazil's largest and most disciplined criminal organisation, functioning as a prison-street gang complex with formal membership, dues and internal courts. Beyond drug trafficking it operates a specialised armed robbery capability responsible for the most sophisticated bank and cash-centre assaults in the Western Hemisphere, and it has expanded into Paraguay, Bolivia and, financially, into Europe. Brazilian prosecutors attribute a share of the novo cangaco raids directly to PCC-linked structures.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: The most capable non-state actor in the world at attacking bank and cash-logistics infrastructure by force. It has demonstrated multi-team assaults on cash centres and vaults involving explosives, drones, human shields and heavy weapons, and it simultaneously represents a first-order money laundering exposure through fuel stations, fintechs and payment institutions in Brazil.
ttps: Multi-team urban raids with 20-40 armed participants seizing a town's police response capacity
Human shields tied to vehicle exteriors to prevent police engagement
Explosive breaching of vaults and ATMs, and drone-assisted overwatch
Disabling of electrical substations and communications before the assault
Deep insider reconnaissance of cash-centre holdings and shift patterns
Laundering through fuel distribution, fintechs and payment institutions
Cross-border staging from Paraguay and Bolivia

existence.basis: Extensive Brazilian prosecutions and academic study.

attribution.basis: Formal membership structure documented judicially.

financial_targeting.basis: Banks, cash centres and CIT are explicit and repeated targets.

actors.name: Novo Cangaco raid crews
actors.description: A distinct Brazilian attack pattern in which a heavily armed crew seizes control of an entire small town for 20 to 60 minutes, neutralising police and communications, in order to strip its bank branches and ATMs. Crews are highly specialised, use assault rifles and explosives, and have taken an estimated USD 120 million since the pattern emerged in 2015. Some raids are attributable to the PCC; many are conducted by independent quadrilhas using the same doctrine.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Defines the worst-case physical scenario for branch networks in low-density areas: the assumption that police response constrains attacker dwell time simply does not hold. It has driven Brazilian banks toward cashless branches, remote vault management and closure of rural cash points, which is itself a financial-inclusion consequence worth tracking.
ttps: Simultaneous seizure of police stations, radio masts and access roads
Suppressive fire from .50 calibre and assault rifles against police facilities
Hostages taken from the street and used as human shields on vehicle exteriors
Explosive breaching of vaults, ATMs and safe rooms
Vehicles burned and roads spiked to block pursuit
Rural dispersal on foot and by boat after the raid

existence.basis: Documented raid series with consistent doctrine; extensive Brazilian reporting and academic analysis.

attribution.basis: Some raids attributed to PCC; many crews are independent and unnamed.

financial_targeting.basis: Bank branches and ATMs are the sole objective of the pattern.

actors.name: Comando Vermelho
actors.description: Brazil's oldest major criminal faction, territorially dominant in Rio de Janeiro favelas and expanding into the Amazon and northern states. Less corporate than the PCC, it exercises territorial control that includes taxation of local commerce and control of utilities and financial services access within its areas.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Territorial control converts into de facto control over who may operate banking correspondents, ATMs and card acceptance in large urban areas. Institutions face extortion of agents, denial of physical access for maintenance and cash replenishment, and customer-level predation. Bank ATMs in controlled territories are routinely stripped or destroyed.

Denial or licensing of access for cash replenishment and maintenance crews
ATM destruction and looting during territorial conflict
Control of local internet and utility provision creating de facto service gatekeeping

actors.name: Brazilian cash-in-transit and cash-logistics attack crews
actors.description: Crews that ambush armoured cash vehicles on highways and, in the highest-capability cases, attack cash vaults and airport cargo areas. Tactics include explosive breaching of the armoured vehicle body, use of heavy weapons to defeat armour, and coordinated blocking of highways. The capability overlaps heavily with the PCC and with novo cangaco crews.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Brazil operates one of the world's largest cash logistics markets, and CIT attack severity there sets the ceiling for what CIT operators globally must design against. Airport cargo attacks additionally implicate bullion and foreign currency movements handled by banks.

actors.name: Brazilian saidinha de banco follow-out robbery cluster
actors.description: Crews that identify customers withdrawing cash inside a branch, follow them out and rob them at the first convenient point. A spotter operates inside the branch or in the queue, communicating by phone to motorcycle-mounted attackers outside. Legislative attention in Brazil has focused on making banks liable for failing to prevent the pattern.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Creates direct legal and reputational liability for banks in Brazil, where courts have repeatedly held institutions responsible for customer losses in follow-out robberies. It is a design problem for branch layout, exit sightlines, cash counting areas and queue privacy rather than a guarding problem.

actors.name: Cartel de Jalisco Nueva Generacion
actors.description: One of Mexico's two dominant cartels, designated a Foreign Terrorist Organization by the United States in 2025 and subject to the largest OFAC action ever taken against it. It fields paramilitary capability including armoured vehicles, drones with explosive payloads and coordinated narcobloqueos, and it operates a professionalised financial arm of money brokers and launderers concentrated in Zapopan and Guadalajara.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Twofold. Operationally, extortion (cobro de piso) reaches bank correspondent agents, ATM operators and armoured transport providers in cartel-controlled states, and vehicle arson and road blockades disrupt cash logistics. Financially, FinCEN has warned US institutions specifically about cartel repatriation of bulk cash through armoured car services and air transport, and the 2025 FTO designation converted routine AML exposure into potential material-support risk.

actors.name: Chinese money laundering organisations in the Americas
actors.description: Broker networks that buy cartel drug cash in North America at a discount and settle the value in China through mirror transfers, using Chinese nationals seeking to move capital out of China as the counterparty. actors.financial_sector_relevance: The dominant laundering methodology now servicing Mexican cartels, and directly relevant to US and Canadian retail banking through structured cash deposits, funnel accounts and trade-account misuse. Physical cash pickups create real robbery and violence risk in branch car parks and around business customers handling the cash.

actors.name: Mexican cobro de piso extortion cluster
actors.description: Systematic extortion of businesses by cartels, splinter groups and freelance criminals across most of Mexico, enforced by arson, kidnapping and murder. Extortion has become a more reliable revenue stream than drug trafficking for many local cells, and it reaches every business type including banking correspondents, ATM operators, armoured transport and fuel retailers.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Creates two hard problems for institutions in Mexico: physical inability to service correspondent agents and ATMs in extorted areas, and account-level patterns of coerced regular cash withdrawals by SME customers that look like laundering but are victimisation. The two require opposite responses, and distinguishing them is a genuine analytical challenge.

actors.name: Tren de Aragua
actors.description: A Venezuelan prison-origin organisation that built a transnational network across Colombia, Peru and Chile between 2018 and 2023, following migration corridors. Designated a transnational criminal organisation by the US Treasury in July 2024 and a Foreign Terrorist Organization in early 2025. Its revenue mix, extortion, migrant smuggling, kidnapping and gota a gota loan sharking, is unusually predatory toward ordinary consumers.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: The primary driver of the regional spread of gota a gota informal lending, which is enforced by violence and which competes directly with regulated consumer credit while generating coerced repayment flows through bank accounts and wallets. Extortion of small businesses across Peru, Chile and Colombia produces the same coerced-withdrawal analytical problem as in Mexico.

actors.name: Gota a gota violent informal lending cluster
actors.description: Daily-repayment informal lending, originally Colombian, now exported across Latin America and into Spain by Colombian and Venezuelan networks. Interest rates are extreme and enforcement is physical: beatings, arson, kidnapping and killings of defaulters. It fills the gap left by limited formal credit access for informal-sector workers.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: The most important consumer-protection-adjacent physical threat in Latin American retail banking. Borrowers frequently use bank accounts, wallets and correspondent agents to make coerced daily repayments, which produces a recognisable transaction signature. It is also a competitive and reputational issue for institutions serving the same segment.

actors.description: Colombia's largest neo-paramilitary organisation, designated a terrorist organisation by the United States in December 2025. actors.name: Viv Ansanm
actors.description: The alliance formed in September 2023 between Haiti's two main gang federations, G-9 and G-Pep, designated a transnational terrorist organisation by the United States in May 2025 and listed by the UN Security Council. actors.name: Argentine salidera bancaria motochorro crews
actors.description: Crews that mark customers inside bank branches, then intercept them on motorcycles at gunpoint after they leave. Argentine cases show a consistent division of labour, with women commonly performing the in-branch marking role and men executing the robbery. Crews use motorcycles, cars and even electric scooters for approach and escape.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: The Argentine analogue of Brazilian saidinha, and a principal driver of Argentine branch-design regulation on privacy screens, cash-counting areas and exit sightlines. High cash usage and periodic currency instability keep large physical withdrawals routine, which sustains the pattern.
ttps: In-branch marker identifying customers making large withdrawals
Communication to motorcycle-mounted attackers outside
Armed interception at the customer's vehicle or first stop
Mixed vehicle fleet including motorcycles, cars and scooters for egress
Repeat targeting of branches with adjacent street parking

existence.basis: Argentine Federal Police operations and prosecutions.

attribution.basis: Specific crews dismantled and charged.

financial_targeting.basis: Victim selection occurs inside bank branches.

actors.name: US jugging crews
actors.description: Crews, heavily associated with Houston-based street gangs but operating across state lines, that surveil banks and cash-heavy businesses, identify a customer or technician carrying cash, follow them and rob them. The mature form of the pattern targets ATM service technicians rather than retail customers, because a technician's vehicle carries cassette-level sums. Federal prosecutions in the Eastern and Northern Districts of Texas have established the model in detail.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: The most operationally significant physical threat to US cash servicing personnel. A technician can be followed across three or four cities before being robbed, meaning the attack happens far from the surveilled branch and outside its security perimeter. Sums involved reach a quarter of a million dollars per event, and the crews travel interstate specifically to defeat local pattern recognition.
ttps: Static surveillance of bank car parks, ATM sites and cash-heavy businesses
Selection of victims observed carrying bags or servicing machines
Multi-vehicle mobile surveillance of ATM technicians across several cities
Armed robbery at a location remote from the observation point
Interstate travel by crews to defeat local intelligence and pattern analysis
Vandalising ATMs with adhesive to force a technician callout, then robbing the responder

existence.basis: Multiple federal convictions and DOJ press releases.

attribution.basis: Named crews charged and convicted, including the Hiram Clarke Money Team.

financial_targeting.basis: Banks, ATMs and cash-servicing personnel are the observation and selection point.

A Houston crew tailed an ATM technician from Irving through Grand Prairie and Arlington before robbing him of roughly USD 250,000 outside a bank.
Two Texas men charged over a national robbery ring that disabled ATMs with adhesive and robbed the responding technicians.

actors.name: ATM technician ambush and induced-callout crews
actors.description: A refinement of jugging in which the crew deliberately disables an ATM, typically by injecting adhesive into the card reader or dispenser, waits for the servicing technician to arrive and open the safe, and then robs them at the open machine. It inverts the defender's assumption that the vulnerable moment is unscheduled; here the attacker chooses the timing.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Turns the maintenance process itself into the attack vector, and defeats controls built around unpredictable replenishment schedules. Mitigation is procedural rather than physical: dual attendance on induced callouts, delay before opening a machine reported as tampered, and treating adhesive faults as a security event rather than a maintenance one.
ttps: Injection of adhesive or foreign objects to force a service callout
Observation of the site until the technician arrives
Armed robbery at the moment the safe is opened
Repeat targeting of the same operator's estate once the response time is known
Nationwide operation by mobile crews

existence.basis: Federal charges and multiple state prosecutions.

attribution.basis: Individual crews charged; the technique is widely copied.

financial_targeting.basis: ATM servicing is the entire premise of the attack.

notable_incidents.summary: Two Texas men charged with conspiracy to commit robbery as part of a national ring that disabled ATMs with a glue-like substance and threatened responding technicians into surrendering cash containers.

watch_indicators: Cluster of adhesive or foreign-object faults across an estate

actors.name: US hook-and-chain and smash-and-grab ATM removal crews
actors.description: Crews that back a pickup truck or SUV to an ATM, attach a chain, and pull the machine out of the ground or the storefront, loading it for later opening. Chicago documented an eleven-location spree in a single campaign. The technique is crude, high-volume and increasingly conducted by large loosely organised groups of eight to twenty who cross state lines.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: The most common destructive attack on the US ATM estate, and a substantial property damage and business interruption cost for host merchants as well as deployers. Anti-ram protection and floor anchoring are the primary controls, and the crews reliably migrate to the softest estate in a region.
ttps: Chain or tow strap attached to the ATM and pulled by a truck or SUV
Night-time and early-morning attacks on standalone and in-store machines
Multi-site sprees within a single metropolitan area
Stolen vehicles used and abandoned
Interstate movement by larger crews

attribution.basis: Crews are transient and often unidentified.

financial_targeting.basis: ATMs are the sole target.

notable_incidents.summary: Burglary crew recorded ripping an ATM from a storefront using a chain and SUV as part of an eleven-location spree.

actors.name: US benefit-card and ATM skimming deployment cluster
actors.description: Deployment crews, predominantly linked to Romanian organised crime, that fit overlay skimmers and pinhole cameras to point-of-sale terminals and ATMs at convenience stores and groceries, targeting magnetic-stripe benefit cards that lack EMV protection. Federal and state cases have produced multi-year sentences and mass arrests, and the technique has spread to states as they roll out benefit programmes.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: A direct demonstration that legacy magnetic-stripe rails attract organised physical attack regardless of the issuer. For banks the read-across is unattended terminal estates and any product still relying on stripe fallback. It also generates significant volumes of victim complaints handled through bank branches even when the issuer is a state agency.
ttps: Overlay skimmers fitted to POS terminals in convenience stores and groceries
Pinhole cameras positioned to capture PIN entry
Deep-insert shimmers at ATMs
Bulk export of harvested card data to cash-out cells
Rapid rotation of deployment personnel across states

actors.name: The Com / IRL Com
actors.description: A primarily English-speaking online ecosystem of interconnected networks, many of whose members are minors, engaged in SIM swapping, intrusion, cryptocurrency theft and extortion. The FBI has issued public warnings about it and estimates thousands of current or recent members. Its critical feature for this database is IRL Com: subgroups that convert online disputes into real-world violence, offering swatting for hire, kidnapping and physical extortion, usually over cryptocurrency.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: The clearest example anywhere of a cyber-native community that has grown a physical violence arm. It directly threatens crypto holders, exchange staff, telecom retail employees recruited for SIM swaps, and increasingly any employee whose credentials give access to customer wealth data. Twelve defendants were sentenced federally over SIM swaps combined with home invasions, which establishes the pattern judicially.
ttps: SIM swapping via bribed or socially engineered telecom retail staff
Home invasion and kidnapping of cryptocurrency holders identified through intrusion data
Swatting for hire, doxxing and violence-for-hire against rivals and victims
Recruitment and coercion of minors as both perpetrators and victims
Insider recruitment at telecoms, exchanges and support providers
Rapid laundering of stolen crypto through mixers and exchanges

existence.basis: FBI IC3 public service announcements and federal prosecutions.

attribution.basis: Individuals are prosecuted; the ecosystem has no membership boundary and subgroups fracture constantly.

financial_targeting.basis: Cryptocurrency theft and extortion are the core activity.

notable_incidents.summary: FBI IC3 public service announcement on The Com, describing theft, extortion and violence as a rising threat to youth online.

actors.name: North American crypto home-invasion and coercion crews
actors.description: Crews that invade the homes of cryptocurrency holders identified through breach data, blockchain analysis or online boasting, and coerce transfers under threat or torture. Frequently overlapping with The Com, but also including conventional armed robbery crews that have adopted the target set because the proceeds are portable, irreversible and non-reportable to a bank.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: The reason self-custody guidance now has to include personal security guidance. For institutions offering custody, wealth management or crypto services, the exposure includes clients, staff with operational key access, and any customer data set that identifies holdings and home addresses.
ttps: Target identification from breach data, chain analysis and social media
Forced entry or impersonation of delivery and utility personnel
Restraint and threat, including violence against family members
Compelled transfers from hardware wallets and exchange accounts
Immediate laundering through mixers and cross-chain swaps

existence.basis: Federal prosecutions and documented incident datasets.

attribution.basis: Crews form per job; overlap with The Com is partial.

financial_targeting.basis: Digital asset holdings determine victim selection.

actors.name: Crypto kiosk-directed victim cluster
actors.description: Networks that direct scam victims, overwhelmingly older adults, to withdraw cash from their bank and deposit it into cryptocurrency kiosks under detailed instruction. The physical element is deliberate: cash withdrawal and kiosk deposit place the irreversible step outside the banking system. FBI IC3 recorded more than 13,400 complaints and over USD 388 million in losses in 2025, with 86 percent of losses among victims aged 60 and over.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Places the bank branch and ATM at the centre of the intervention opportunity, because the withdrawal precedes the irreversible deposit. Several US states have now banned or capped kiosks, which is a direct regulatory consequence. Institutions offering kiosk operators banking services also carry reputational and AML exposure.
ttps: Impersonation of government, bank or technical support to establish urgency
Step-by-step coaching through bank withdrawal, kiosk location and deposit
Instruction to conceal the purpose from bank staff
Use of kiosks with weak identity verification and high transaction limits
Immediate onward transfer from the receiving wallet

existence.basis: FBI IC3 annual reporting and state legislative response.

attribution.basis: Perpetrators are largely offshore and unidentified.

financial_targeting.basis: Bank withdrawals and crypto kiosks are integral to the method.

notable_incidents.summary: FBI IC3 recorded over 13,400 crypto kiosk complaints with losses exceeding USD 388 million; adults 60 and over accounted for 86 percent of reported losses.
Minnesota banned crypto kiosks statewide following similar restrictions in Indiana and Tennessee.

watch_indicators: Older customer withdrawing an atypical cash sum with a rehearsed explanation

actors.name: Felony Lane Gang
actors.description: A loosely affiliated network, originating in Florida, that burglarises vehicles at gyms, parks and daycare centres to steal handbags containing chequebooks and identity documents, then uses disguised female couriers to cash the cheques at the outermost drive-through lane of bank branches, chosen because it is furthest from the teller's view. The name derives from that lane.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: A rare example of a physical crime pattern engineered specifically around a bank's own service channel design. It exploits drive-through identity verification weakness at scale across state lines, and it remains a persistent cheque fraud and branch procedure problem in the United States and Canada.
ttps: Vehicle burglary at gyms, parks, daycare centres and trailheads
Theft of chequebooks, identity documents and debit cards
Use of wigs and disguises by couriers to match stolen identity documents
Presentation at the outermost drive-through lane to exploit poor visual verification
Interstate travel in rented vehicles, hitting many branches per day

existence.basis: Extensive US and Canadian police reporting and prosecutions.

attribution.basis: A method and affiliation label rather than a hierarchical organisation.

financial_targeting.basis: Bank drive-through channels are the designed exploitation point.

watch_indicators: Cluster of vehicle burglaries at recreational sites preceding cheque presentations

actors.name: Air cargo and bullion insider-facilitated theft cluster
actors.description: Theft of high-value cargo, principally bullion and foreign currency, from airport cargo facilities using insider access and forged documentation rather than force. The April 2023 Toronto Pearson theft of over CAD 20 million in gold and foreign currency, executed with a fraudulent airway bill and the cooperation of airline employees, is the reference case; ten people were charged, including current and former airline staff.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Bullion and currency shipments are a core banking logistics function and the weakest link is documentary control at the cargo handover, not the vault. It is also a striking insider case: the theft required no weapons, only a plausible document and someone willing to accept it. Recovered proceeds were minimal because the gold was melted down within days.
ttps: Fraudulent airway bills presented to cargo handling staff
Recruitment of current and former airline employees
Rapid removal by truck before reconciliation
Immediate melting of bullion to defeat serial identification
Laundering of proceeds through jewellery businesses

existence.basis: Canadian charges against ten individuals and subsequent civil litigation.

attribution.basis: Named defendants including airline employees.

financial_targeting.basis: Bank-consigned bullion and currency shipments were the target.

notable_incidents.summary: Over CAD 20 million in gold (6,600 bars) and about CAD 2.5 million in foreign currency removed using a fraudulent airway bill; ten charged including current and former Air Canada employees. Only melted-down remnants worth CAD 89,000 recovered.
Federal Court ordered Air Canada to pay Brink's just over CAD 18,000 for the shipment, illustrating the contractual liability gap.

actors.name: MS-13 and Barrio 18
actors.description: Central American street gangs whose economic base is neighbourhood extortion of businesses, transport operators and residents. El Salvador's state of exception since 2022 has severely degraded their operational capacity there, displacing activity toward Guatemala and Honduras. In the United States they remain a local violent crime problem rather than a financial one.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Extortion of small businesses and transport is collected largely in cash and increasingly through mobile wallets and bank transfers, producing recognisable coerced-payment patterns. Remittance agents and microfinance branches in affected neighbourhoods face both extortion and robbery risk, and the customer base's ability to repay loans is directly affected by extortion load.

Enforcement by murder and arson against non-payers
Collection via cash, mobile wallets and third-party accounts
Territorial control restricting access for service providers
Prison-based coordination of collection

existence.basis: Extensive US and Central American designations and prosecutions.

attribution.basis: Well-defined gang identities.

financial_targeting.basis: Extortion reaches financial service agents and customers; institutions are not attacked directly.

watch_indicators: Microfinance and remittance agents reporting extortion demands

actors.name: US anti-government and anti-corporate extremist cluster targeting financial institutions
actors.description: A heterogeneous set of US ideological actors whose grievances converge on financial institutions: sovereign citizen adherents who file fraudulent liens and instruments and occasionally threaten bank staff, anti-capitalist and anti-development direct action cells that attack branches associated with disfavoured projects, and lone actors motivated by debt or foreclosure grievance. Attacks are typically arson, vandalism or threats rather than organised campaigns.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Produces the majority of ideologically motivated physical incidents at US bank premises, most of them low severity, plus a persistent stream of paper terrorism (bogus liens, fictitious instruments) that consumes legal and operations resource. Threats to named staff, particularly in foreclosure and collections roles, are the main personnel safety concern.

Filing of fraudulent liens and fictitious financial instruments against staff and institutions
Threats and harassment directed at named employees in collections and foreclosure
Occupation and disruption of branch lobbies

actors.name: US armoured car and cash-logistics robbery cluster
actors.description: Crews that attack armoured car crews at the pavement transfer point, the moment when cash or valuables are outside the vehicle and the guard is exposed. Unlike the Italian or Brazilian pattern there is little use of explosives or heavy weapons; the US pattern is ambush at the point of transfer, frequently with inside information about the run. High-value jewellery and bullion loads have also been targeted at rest stops during long-haul movements.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: The principal armed threat to US cash logistics. The consistent finding across cases is that the transfer point and the predictable stop, not the vehicle, is the vulnerability, and that insider knowledge of load value features in the largest events.
ttps: Ambush at the pavement transfer point during ATM or branch servicing
Targeting of predictable rest stops on long-haul high-value runs
Insider tipping on load composition and value
Rapid vehicle switch and dispersal
Occasional use of impersonation to approach the crew

existence.basis: Sustained FBI and federal prosecution record.

attribution.basis: Crews are transient; few persistent organisations.

financial_targeting.basis: Cash and valuables in transit are the sole target.

watch_indicators: Observation of crews at transfer points reported by guards
Route and stop predictability on high-value runs
Insider access to load manifests outside role requirements

actors.name: Peruvian extortion networks
actors.description: Fragmented Peruvian extortion cells, concentrated in Lima, Trujillo and northern coastal cities, that target transport operators, construction firms and small businesses. Enforcement uses grenades and improvised explosives against premises and vehicles, and Venezuelan networks including TdA-linked cells have entered the same market. Peru declared states of emergency in response.
actors.financial_sector_relevance: Extortion payment demands are increasingly made through bank transfers and wallets rather than cash, which puts institutions in the position of processing the payment leg of a violent crime. Small business customers under extortion show characteristic repeated transfers to individual accounts, and their creditworthiness is affected directly.

Grenade and IED attacks on non-paying businesses and transport vehicles
Contract killing of resistant business owners
Collection via bank transfer, wallet and money service business
Prison-based coordination of extortion campaigns
